questions.question: Brake fading happens when:

options.text: Brakes are not used often enough.

questions.explanation: Using brakes too much causes them to overheat. When brakes overheat, they become less effective. This is called fading.

questions.question: During an inspection, slack adjusters on S-cam brakes should not move more than:
questions.explanation: Park on level ground and set wheel chocks. Pull each slack adjuster to check movement. They should not move more than one inch. If they move more than one inch, they need adjustment.

questions.question: Which one is not a type of retarder?
questions.explanation: Retarders help slow a vehicle and reduce brake use. The four types are exhaust, engine, hydraulic, and electric.

questions.question: Air tank drains:

options.text: Should not be used in cold weather.
Help remove water and oil from the air tanks.
Are used to move air to the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains water and oil. These can damage the brake system if they build up. Air tanks have drain valves to remove water and oil.

questions.question: When backing up, it is best to:

options.text: Rely only on the passenger's side mirror.
Turn toward the passenger's side whenever possible.

questions.explanation: Back up slowly and use both mirrors. Have a helper watch your blind spots when possible. Agree on a signal that means stop.

questions.question: The steering wheel should be:

options.text: Held with one hand to allow eating and drinking.
Held by one hand at a time, switching hands.

questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands for proper control. Place your hands on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Make sure your glasses are clean.

questions.explanation: Do not wear sunglasses when driving at night. They reduce your vision. Keep eyeglasses clean and scratch-free. Get enough rest before driving at night.

questions.question: When uncoupling, the landing gear should be:
questions.explanation: Before driving, raise the landing gear completely. When uncoupling, lower the landing gear until it is firmly on the ground. If the trailer is loaded, turn the crank extra times to remove some weight.

questions.question: When approaching a vehicle for a pre-trip inspection, look under it to:

options.text: See if the vehicle is on an incline.
See if the vehicle is in a parking spot.

questions.explanation: Look under the vehicle for fresh leaks of oil, grease, or fuel. Check the area around the vehicle for hazards like people, other vehicles, or low wires.

questions.question: Which of the following could reduce the clearance between the road and an overhead object like a bridge?
questions.explanation: Do not assume bridge height signs are exact. If the road was repaved after the sign was posted, or if snow is on the ground, the actual clearance may be different.

questions.question: Having ABS on only one axle:

options.text: Still gives you better control when braking.
Slows the vehicle, but cannot stop it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Still gives you better control when braking.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) on only the tractor, only the trailer, or only one axle, you will still have more control when braking than without ABS. Brake normally.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of a vehicle's air brake system?
questions.explanation: Air brake system parts include: air compressor, air compressor governor, air storage tanks, air tank drains, alcohol evaporator, safety valve, brake pedal, foundation brakes, supply pressure gauges, application pressure gauge, low air pressure warning signal, stop light switch, front brake limiting valve, spring brakes, and parking brake controls.

questions.question: Antifreeze helps an engine work properly:
questions.explanation: Always keep enough water and antifreeze in your cooling system. Despite its name, antifreeze helps your engine even in hot weather.

questions.question: What is the average driver's reaction time?

options.text: Between three-quarters and one full second

questions.correctAnswerText: Between three-quarters and one full second
questions.explanation: The average driver's reaction time is between three-quarters of a second and one full second.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve:

options.text: Should always be used for parking.
Should only be used for parking on a downhill.
Should never be used for parking.
Should only be used when transporting cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should never be used for parking.
questions.explanation: Do not use the trailer hand valve for parking. It can cause all air to leak out of the braking system, which releases the brakes. Use the parking brake instead.

questions.question: When coupling a trailer:

options.text: Connect the correct glad hands to each other.
Any glad hands can be connected together.
Only one set of glad hands should be connected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connect the correct glad hands to each other.
questions.explanation: Connect matching glad hands when coupling. They are often color-coded to help you avoid mistakes. Blue is usually for service lines and red is usually for emergency lines.

questions.question: Which type of vehicle is most prone to the "crack-the-whip" effect?
questions.explanation: Double and triple combinations are most likely to turn over from the "crack-the-whip" effect.

questions.question: When driving a double or triple, remember that:

options.text: The vehicle needs more space than most other vehicles.
Other drivers will always get out of your way.
The vehicle weighs about the same as other vehicles.
The vehicle easily fits into small spaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle needs more space than most other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Doubles and triples need more space than other vehicles because they are longer and cannot turn or stop quickly. Always make sure you have enough space before entering traffic, crossing traffic, or changing lanes.

questions.question: If a speed limit is posted:

options.text: You can exceed it when passing another vehicle.
You can exceed it in a rural area.

questions.explanation: A posted speed limit is the fastest you can legally drive under ideal conditions. You must slow down as needed based on conditions. Never exceed the legal speed limit.

questions.question: Which surface provides the least traction?
questions.explanation: Be very careful when driving on melting ice. Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice.
